key_insight: At affordable mesh resolutions, a single fracture-model parameter set cannot simultaneously match elastic slope, peak force and crack path in cooled dark chocolate.
engineering_relevance: Predicting brittle-food breakage requires calibration tailored to the target property, such as failure load or fragment geometry.
method: Assess sharp-interface and diffuse phase-field models for Griffith-type brittle fracture.
Identify elastic parameters from pre-crack tension and compression, then critical energy release rate from three-point-bending peak force.
Calibrate phase-field width last and report the calibration objective, numerical settings and boundary value problem.
evidence_signal: The cooled-dark-chocolate case study assesses both frameworks at affordable spatial discretization, using staged loading responses to identify parameters.
watch_item: Mesh resolution constrains phase-field width, which influences structural response, crack curvature and stress fields.
paper_title: Finite Element Modeling of Fracture in Brittle Foods with Physically Consistent Parameter Calibration: A Practical Case Study on Cooled Dark Chocolate
